customer: Embedded developers, validation engineers and small NPI/test teams that need repeatable low-speed SPI/I2C interaction without paying several hundred dollars for a professional host adapter/programmer.
positioning: A protected, scriptable USB-C SPI/I2C validation pod between bare hobby bridges and professional $275-$375 tools.

economics.note: These are design targets, not supplier quotes.

candidate_architecture.target_power_switch: TPS2553DBVR active-high adjustable current-limited switch with reverse-voltage protection
candidate_architecture.target_current_limit_programming: 133k 1% RILIM; ~201.5mA nominal and ~233.9mA datasheet maximum before resistor tolerance
candidate_architecture.target_supply: physical 1.8V/3.3V selection before electronically disabled target-power switch
protection: target-line series resistance pending exact values
target connector ESD pending exact part
candidate_architecture.connector_strategy: keyed primary target connector plus simple breakout adapter; exact MPN pending

evidence_receipt.rule: A successful protocol call is not sufficient by itself; the receipt must bind the transaction to the exact pod revision, firmware and target-power state.

explicit_non_goals_v0: autonomous write/erase without physical user arm
next_gate: GitHub Actions must generate the editable KiCad schematic, export the netlist, pass the explicit safety-topology checks, and return zero ERC violations before PCB work can open.
